'''Cullen skink''' is a thick [[Scottish cuisine|Scottish]] [[soup]] typically made of at least smoked [[haddock]], [[potato|potatoes]], and [[onion]]s.<ref name="f788">{{cite book | last=Marco | first=Pasquale De | title=Edinburgh and the Scottish Highlands: A Guide for the Curious | publisher=Pasquale De Marco | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ZotJEQAAQBAJ&dq=Cullen+skink&pg=PA122 | access-date=2025-10-21}}</ref> An authentic Cullen skink will use [[finnan haddie]], but it may be prepared with any other undyed [[smoking (cooking)|smoked]] haddock. Sometimes [[ocean perch]] or [[salmon]] are used in the soup. It is often served as a starter at formal Scottish dinners but is also widely served as a common dish across Scotland, especially in the northeast.<ref name="j521">{{cite book | last=Gibson | first=Rebecca | title=North East Scotland (Slow Travel): including Aberdeenshire, Moray and the Cairngorms National Park | publisher=Bradt Travel Guides | date=2023-05-15 | isbn=978-1-78477-901-6 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Q7MYEQAAQBAJ&dq=Cullen+skink&pg=PA18 | access-date=2025-10-21 | page=18}}</ref> Cullen skink appears in many traditional Scottish cookery books and restaurant and hotel menus throughout Scotland, the rest of the UK and abroad.<ref name="m847">{{cite book | last=Guides | first=Fodor's Travel | title=Fodor's Essential Scotland | publisher=Fodor's Travel | date=2022-06-21 | isbn=978-1-64097-497-5 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=rW1xEAAAQBAJ&dq=Cullen+skink&pg=PT36 | access-date=2025-10-21}}</ref>
